title: M5 stage36: finite binary recovery driven by completion counts
scope: Explicit structurally terminating binary branch algorithm and its generic count-partition correctness; arithmetic completion-count instantiation remains required.

spec.name: M5.BinaryRecovery.recover_length
spec.statement: ∀ (c : List Bool → ℤ) (p : List Bool) (n : ℕ), (M5.BinaryRecovery.recover c p n).length = p.length + n
spec.guidance: Induct n generalizing p; unfold recover and split the if. List.length_append gives one additional decision each step. This algorithm evaluates the false branch count once and recurses with one fewer undecided position. Return only tactic lines without leading by; preserve exact statement.

spec.name: M5.BinaryRecovery.recover_positive
spec.statement: ∀ (c : List Bool → ℤ) (p : List Bool) (n : ℕ), (∀ q : List Bool, q.length < p.length + n → c q = c (q ++ [false]) + c (q ++ [true])) → 0 < c p → 0 < c (M5.BinaryRecovery.recover c p n)
spec.guidance: Induct n generalizing p. At successor, the split law applies atp. If false-child count>0 use it; otherwise parent positivity and count split force true-child count>0 by omega. For the recursive split hypothesis, the length bound (p++[bit]).length+n equals p.length+(n+1). No global nonnegative assumption is needed. Return only tactic lines without leading by; preserve exact statement.

spec.name: M5.BinaryRecovery.recover_valid
spec.statement: ∀ (c : List Bool → ℤ) (Valid : List Bool → Prop) (m : ℕ), (∀ q : List Bool, q.length < m → c q = c (q ++ [false]) + c (q ++ [true])) → (∀ q : List Bool, q.length = m → 0 < c q → Valid q) → 0 < c [] → (M5.BinaryRecovery.recover c [] m).length = m ∧ Valid (M5.BinaryRecovery.recover c [] m)
spec.guidance: Apply recover_length atempty prefix and recover_positive. The terminal correctness premise then gives Valid. This is a generic algorithm theorem; later instantiate c by the proven arithmetic completion count and Valid by physical recipe validity. Do not replace c with enumeration. Return only tactic lines without leading by; preserve exact statement.
